title: UNIT 5: CIRCLES
notes:
✓ Circle → the set of all points in a plane that are equidistant from a fixed point called the center.

✓ Radius (r) → distance from the center to any point on the circle.

✓ Diameter (d) → chord passing through the center; d = 2r.

✓ Circumference → perimeter of a circle; C = 2πr.

✓ Area → A = πr².

title: 5.1 SYMMETRICAL PROPERTIES OF CIRCLES
notes:
✓ Symmetry → a figure has symmetry when one half coincides with the other half after folding.

✓ Every diameter of a circle is a line of symmetry.

✓ A circle has infinitely many lines of symmetry because every diameter can act as a line of symmetry.

✓ Key idea → corresponding points on opposite sides of a line of symmetry are equally distant from that line.

Example: Folding a circle along any diameter produces two equal semicircles.

title: PARTS OF A CIRCLE
notes:
✓ Center → fixed point from which all points on the circle are equally distant.

✓ Radius → line segment from center to circumference.

✓ Diameter → chord passing through the center.

✓ Chord → line segment joining two points on a circle.

✓ Arc → part of the circumference.

✓ Tangent → line that meets a circle at exactly one point.

✓ Secant → line that intersects a circle at two points.

✓ Diameter = 2 × radius.
✓ Circumference = 2πr.
✓ Area = πr².

title: CHARACTERISTICS OF CHORDS
notes:
✓ Theorem → The line segment joining the center of a circle to the midpoint of a chord is perpendicular to the chord.

✓ Theorem → A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

✓ Theorem → Equal chords of a circle are equidistant from the center.

✓ Theorem → Equal chords subtend equal angles at the center.

✓ Converse → Equal central angles subtend equal chords.

Example: If a chord is 8 cm and the radius is 5 cm, half the chord is 4 cm. Using Pythagoras:
d = √(5² − 4²) = √9 = 3 cm.

Here d is the distance from the center to the chord.

title: CHORD–CENTER RELATIONSHIP
notes:
When a perpendicular is drawn from the center O to chord AB at M:

✓ AM = MB.
✓ OM ⟂ AB.
✓ OA = OB = radius.

Using the right triangle OMA:
✓ OA² = OM² + AM²

Therefore:
✓ OM = √(r² − (AB/2)²).

Example: r = 5 cm and AB = 8 cm:
OM = √(25 − 16) = 3 cm.

title: 5.2 ANGLE PROPERTIES OF CIRCLES
notes:
◆ Minor arc → arc measuring less than 180°.

◆ Major arc → arc measuring more than 180°.

◆ Semicircle → arc measuring 180°.

✓ Central angle → angle whose vertex is at the center and whose sides are radii.

✓ Inscribed angle → angle whose vertex lies on the circle and whose sides are chords.

✓ Central angle and its intercepted arc have the same measure.

title: CENTRAL & INSCRIBED ANGLES
notes:
✓ Theorem → If a central angle and an inscribed angle intercept the same arc, then:

Inscribed angle = 1/2 × central angle.

Therefore:
✓ Central angle = 2 × inscribed angle.

Example: If a central angle is 100° and both angles intercept the same arc:
Inscribed angle = 100°/2 = 50°.

title: ANGLES SUBTENDED BY THE SAME ARC
notes:
✓ Theorem → Inscribed angles subtended by the same arc have equal measures.

Example:
If ∠ACB and ∠ADB intercept the same arc AB and ∠ACB = 45°, then:
∠ADB = 45°.

This property is useful when several points lie on the circumference of the same circle.

title: ANGLE IN A SEMICIRCLE — THALES' THEOREM
notes:
✓ Thales' Theorem → An angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle.

Therefore:
If AB is a diameter and C lies on the circle, then:
∠ACB = 90°.

Example: If AB is a diameter and ∠ABC = 55°:
∠ACB = 90°
∠BAC = 180° − 90° − 55° = 35°.

title: CYCLIC QUADRILATERAL
notes:
✓ Cyclic quadrilateral → a quadrilateral whose four vertices lie on the same circle.

✓ Theorem → Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary.

Therefore:
✓ ∠A + ∠C = 180°
✓ ∠B + ∠D = 180°

✓ Sum of all four angles = 360°.

Example:
If one angle is 108°, its opposite angle is:
180° − 108° = 72°.

title: TANGENTS TO A CIRCLE
notes:
✓ Tangent → a line that meets a circle at exactly one point called the point of tangency.

✓ A tangent at a point on a circle is perpendicular to the radius drawn to that point.

Therefore:
radius ⟂ tangent
and the angle between them = 90°.

✓ Tangent segments drawn from the same external point to a circle are equal.

Example: If PA and PB are tangents from P and PA = 7 cm, then PB = 7 cm.

title: 5.3 ARC LENGTH
notes:
✓ Arc length → the length of a portion of the circumference.

For radius r and central angle θ in degrees:

✓ Arc length:
s = 2πr × θ/360°

Since d = 2r:
s = πd × θ/360°

Example: If r = 6 cm and θ = 60°:
s = 2π(6)(60/360)
= 2π cm.

title: SECTOR OF A CIRCLE
notes:
✓ Sector → a region of a circle enclosed by two radii and an arc.

◆ Minor sector → central angle is less than 180°.
◆ Major sector → central angle is greater than 180°.

✓ Area of sector:
A = πr² × θ/360°

✓ Perimeter of sector:
P = 2r + arc length

P = 2r + 2πr × θ/360°.

title: SECTOR — EXAMPLE
notes:
Example: r = 6 cm and θ = 210°.

Area:
A = π(6²)(210/360)
= 21π cm².

Arc length:
s = 2π(6)(210/360)
= 7π cm.

Perimeter:
P = 2(6) + 7π
= 12 + 7π cm.

title: SEGMENT OF A CIRCLE
notes:
✓ Segment → region enclosed by a chord and its corresponding arc.

✓ Area of a segment:
Area of segment = Area of sector − Area of triangle.

✓ Formula when the central angle is θ:
Asegment = πr²(θ/360°) − 1/2 r²sinθ.

Example: If sector area = 100 m² and triangle area = 78 m²:
Segment area = 100 − 78 = 22 m².

title: PERIMETER OF A SEGMENT
notes:
✓ The perimeter of a segment consists of:

◆ 1. The chord.
◆ 2. The corresponding arc.

Therefore:
✓ Perimeter of segment = chord length + arc length.

Always identify both the straight boundary and curved boundary before calculating the perimeter.

title: CHORD INTERSECTION INSIDE A CIRCLE
notes:
When two chords intersect inside a circle, they form angles whose measures depend on the intercepted arcs.

✓ Theorem → The measure of an angle formed by two intersecting chords inside a circle is:

Angle = 1/2 × (sum of intercepted arcs).

✓ Formula:
∠ = 1/2(arc₁ + arc₂).

Example: If the intercepted arcs are 68° and 128°:
∠ = 1/2(68 + 128)
= 98°.

title: INTERSECTING CHORDS — PRODUCT THEOREM
notes:
✓ When two chords intersect inside a circle, the products of the two pairs of chord segments are equal.

✓ Formula:
AP × PB = CP × PD.

Example: If AP = 3 cm, PB = 8 cm and CP = 4 cm:
3 × 8 = 4 × PD
24 = 4PD
PD = 6 cm.

title: SECANTS & TANGENTS OUTSIDE A CIRCLE
notes:
✓ Secant → a line that intersects the circle at two points.
✓ Tangent → a line that intersects the circle at one point.

✓ Theorem → When two secants, two tangents, or a secant and a tangent intersect outside a circle, the angle formed equals half the positive difference of the intercepted arcs.

✓ Formula:
Angle = 1/2 × (larger arc − smaller arc).

Example: If intercepted arcs are 107° and 43°:
Angle = 1/2(107 − 43)
= 32°.

title: UNIT 5 KEY THEOREMS
notes:
✓ 1. A perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

✓ 2. Equal chords are equidistant from the center.

✓ 3. Equal chords subtend equal central angles.

✓ 4. Equal central angles subtend equal chords.

✓ 5. An inscribed angle is half the central angle intercepting the same arc.

✓ 6. Inscribed angles subtending the same arc are equal.

✓ 7. An angle in a semicircle is 90°.

✓ 8. Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°.

✓ 9. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency.

✓ 10. Tangents from the same external point are equal.

✓ 11. Intersecting chords inside: angle = 1/2(sum of arcs).

✓ 12. External secant/tangent angles: angle = 1/2(difference of arcs).

✓ 13. Intersecting chords: AP × PB = CP × PD.

title: UNIT 5 QUICK FORMULA SHEET
notes:
✓ Diameter: d = 2r
✓ Circumference: C = 2πr
✓ Area: A = πr²

✓ Arc length:
s = 2πr(θ/360°)

✓ Sector area:
A = πr²(θ/360°)

✓ Sector perimeter:
P = 2r + 2πr(θ/360°)

✓ Segment area:
Asegment = Asector − Atriangle

✓ Central/inscribed angle:
Inscribed angle = 1/2 central angle

✓ Semicircle:
Angle = 90°

✓ Cyclic quadrilateral:
Opposite angles = 180°

✓ Chords intersecting inside:
Angle = 1/2(sum of intercepted arcs)

✓ Secants/tangents outside:
Angle = 1/2(difference of intercepted arcs)

✓ Chord products:
AP × PB = CP × PD.
